prize_parts.citation: For the rational design of zeolite and molecular-sieve catalysts with controlled pore architectures and active sites

statement.case_for: Zeolite and molecular-sieve design is the clearest case on the shortlist of structure determining function and of that relationship being exploited by design. Organic structure-directing agents (Zones' SSZ-13 and related frameworks), synthesis strategy and framework design (Davis), and tailored active sites with industrial translation (Corma) turned an empirical craft into a rational one. The result is used at very large scale in cracking, methanol-to-olefins and NOx emission control. The structures were determined and the structure-property links are verified, not narrated, and the principle has fed straight into MOF, COF and other porous-framework chemistry. Maturity is not in doubt: decades of independent confirmation across academia and industry. This is also a chemistry prize in the strict sense, with no overlap with a prior prize in another field.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is that this is a broad research programme and not a single discovery, so a short citation and a clean three-name attribution are hard to write, and several equally strong zeolite scientists fall outside or at the edge of the credited set (Tsapatsis and Yu are on the ballot but not in my trio). No other member ranked B033 in their opening top eight, so I have no evidence that it can reach five votes, and I am wary that my own field proximity inflates my view of it. Candidates with a sharper single event, such as base editing, have a simpler story to tell.

responses.point: Nitrogenase (B012) is the kind of mechanism-in-physical-terms problem he values most. He supports Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt on the structure of FeMo-cofactor and the kinetic framework, and acknowledges that the mechanism at the cofactor is still debated.
responses.response: I agree the structural work is excellent, and the interstitial carbide is a real crystallographic result that I take seriously. That is also my reservation. The structure is secure, but the question that makes it a mechanism prize, where N2 binds and what the E4 hydride state is, is by your own account not closed. Rewarding the structure now while the mechanism is open risks a citation that overstates what was shown. I rank it sixth for that reason. Attribution among Dean, Rees, Seefeldt, Einsle and Ribbe is also hard with only three places. If the committee waits for the turnover-state structures to settle the mechanism, I would support it.

responses.point: He puts base editing (B062) first and proposes David Liu alone. He argues that Liu is the intellectual driver of both editors, that this keeps the prize simple, and that it avoids splitting credit with CRISPR-Cas9 (2020).
responses.response: I am sympathetic to base editing as a chemist's invention and ranked it third, so it is my first alternative. I would qualify the single-laureate proposal. The adenine base editor required directed evolution of a new TadA deaminase, which was Gaudelli's decisive step, and Kondo and Nishida's independent deaminase-fusion work is a competing claim that cannot be dismissed. Naming Liu alone is defensible as a judgement but I would want the committee to say explicitly why it excludes those contributions, and not merely say it is simpler. I also doubt that clinical durability is known well enough yet. I would still call this the strongest of the biology-facing candidates.

responses.point: He ranks Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling (B039) first with Hartwig and Buchwald. He values a clear, general mechanistic principle with enormous practical use, and notes a mild overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
responses.response: Our views are close in spirit, since we both give weight to a general design principle with large industrial use. B039 is a strong, mature candidate and I do not think the 2010 overlap is disqualifying, because ligand-controlled C-N coupling is a different bond construction with distinct catalyst design. Where I differ is on ranking: I think zeolite design shows the same kind of rational, ligand-or-template-controlled design principle in the solid state, and it has had no recognition at all. I would be content to see B039 as a serious competitor and would not oppose it.

responses.point: She ranks biomolecular condensates (B036) first, as a physically grounded concept of membraneless organisation with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as the natural trio.
responses.response: The concept is important and I accept the physical-chemical framing. My reservation is evidentiary, as you partly note. For many condensates the claim that they are truly liquid and functionally required in cells rests on indirect imaging and in vitro reconstitution, and the structural basis of the multivalent interactions is thin. I want to know whether what is claimed has been shown at molecular resolution. That makes the maturity less settled for me than for the materials candidates, and a chemistry citation would have to be narrowly worded. I would not block it, but I would want that debate resolved first.

uncertainties: Whether B033 can be written as one coherent prize-worthy achievement and not a broad research area, and whether Corma, Davis and Zones are the right trio against Tsapatsis, Yu and others.
Whether any other member will give B033 serious weight, since I currently have no support for it and may need to move to a configuration that can reach five votes.
Whether the committee prefers a biology-facing prize (B062, B066, B036) or a materials/synthesis one this year.
For B031, whether stability and lead content, and the physics framing, weaken its chemistry case, and whether a three-name cut among six credited people is acceptable.
statement.conflict_note: My own research field (zeolites, MOFs and porous framework materials, with structure determination of zeolites by electron crystallography) is very close to B033 and also to the porous-materials side of B031's materials community. The profile names no specific collaboration with Corma, Davis, Zones, Yu or Tsapatsis, but as a member of this research community I may well have professional connections, so recusal on B033 deserves consideration if the committee finds a closer link. No other specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile.
